title: eval-notice-prioritization-and-compact-threading-for-console-alerts
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: Evals produce a high volume of quality-change notices after model/config rollouts. On-call and product teams see many near-duplicate alerts for the same underlying regression (slightly different metrics, per-eval snapshots), which increases noise and slows response. Current dedupe groups exist but are noisy and often surface low-priority regressions as separate incidents.

Goal: Implement a prioritization + compact-threading model in Console so that related eval-change notices are consolidated into a single compact alert thread (Slack/PagerDuty) with a prioritized summary. Prioritization should be latency-aware (higher weight for regressions affecting 95p latency and unit cost impact) and sensitive to model/config diffs (fingerprint by model version + config hash + eval-suite). PagerDuty should only receive incidents above a configurable severity threshold.

Scope: Console backend and alerting pipeline changes (fingerprinting, scoring), notification adapters for Slack and PagerDuty (compact summary + actionable links), UI affordance in Console for viewing grouped notices and promoting/dismissing them, acceptance criteria and rollout plan.

Out of scope: Major eval rearchitecture, deep changes to eval metrics themselves (we will use existing metric definitions), new on-call playbooks (ops will extend after release).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Notices from related eval diffs (same model+config+eval suite within 24h) are grouped into one compact thread in Slack with a single stub message and up to 5 inline snapshots.
2) PagerDuty incidents are created only for grouped notices with computed severity >= 0.7 (configurable).
3) Console UI shows a single grouped notice with clear rollup score, contributing snapshots, and links to the eval diff and model rollout page.
4) Noise metric: daily alert volume for eval-change notices reduces by >=40% in the first 2 weeks in canary orgs.
5) On-call feedback (survey) rates this flow >=4/5 for signal relevance in canary customers.
6) No customer-facing regressions (false suppressions) observed in canary window; automated fallback sends suppressed notices to internal archive for review.
design_notes:
- Threading key = hash(model_version + config_hash + eval_suite_id + time_bucket(24h)).
- Scoring = weighted sum: severity_delta*0.6 + latency_impact*0.25 + traffic_exposure*0.15. Weights tunable via feature flag.
- Compact Slack message: header (model, env, score), 3-line summary, expandable block with top 5 snapshots (metric, delta, sparkline), link to Console diff. Use thread replies for follow-ups.
- PagerDuty mapping: score>=threshold -> create incident with dedupe_key = threading key; lower severity -> send to a dedicated Slack channel only.
- UI: grouped notice card shows contributors (collapsed by default), primary metric, suggested severity and recommended action (rollback/monitor).
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (backend + webhook): fingerprinting service + scoring function + provide webhook envelope changes. Phase 2 (Slack/PagerDuty adapters): send compact stub messages, attach eval snapshot links, ensure PagerDuty dedupe_key used. Phase 3 (Console UI): grouped notice card, controls for ungrouping and adjusting threshold. Phase 4 (Canary rollout + telemetry): enable for 3 internal orgs, collect noise/precision metrics and survey.

API/PRs: initial hashing and scoring PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10894
Webhook schema change RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Notification+Envelope+v2
Slack UX mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3_mockup
PagerDuty playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Eval+Alerting+PD+Runbook
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Over-aggressive grouping could suppress distinct regressions. Mitigation: keep grouping conservative (24h window) and expose 'ungroup' action in UI; send suppressed notices to internal archive.
- Risk: Scoring model misses customer priorities. Mitigation: configurable weights, canary feedback loop, per-customer overrides.
- Risk: PagerDuty dedupe misfires across multiple services. Mitigation: include account_id and service_id in dedupe key and test in staging PD account.
- Risk: Slack rate limits for large orgs. Mitigation: use batched updates and ephemeral message strategy; monitor and backoff.
metrics:
- Alert volume (daily) for eval-change notices (pre/post).
- Percent of notices grouped (target >=60%).
- PagerDuty incidents triggered per day (reduce low-severity incidents by >=50%).
- Mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) for high-severity grouped incidents.
- False suppression rate (notices suppressed but later ungrouped by humans).
